claim.text: We created an OAuth connection and its authorization URL worked straight away. Only a Marketplace listing needs Notion's review.

evidence.quote: Creating the connection took one submission. Notion showed no review step, no CAPTCHA and no email confirmation.
You can create and use a public connection without listing it.

summary: Self-serve, and we tested it: one form creates an OAuth connection that works right away. A Marketplace listing is optional, needs a security review, and Notion says to expect an answer in 5 to 10 business days. Two things trip people up: the installation scope cannot be changed after creation, and unlike GitHub only the exact registered redirect URI works.

composio.note: Composio lists a managed OAuth app for Notion. You may not need your own unless you want your own branding, scopes beyond the defaults, or dedicated rate limits.

evidence.quote: Composio-managed OAuth available

effort.text: 0.5-1 hours to set up the app (our estimate: create the connection, pick its scope and capabilities, wire up the redirect; excludes the Marketplace listing)

wait.text: Marketplace listing only: Notion says to expect to hear back within 5-10 business days. Using the connection without listing it needs no wait.

evidence.quote: After submission, expect to hear back from our team within 5-10 business days via email.

claim.text: low to use, medium for a Marketplace listing (our judgment: a short review, but rejections are possible)

scopeTiers.text: Installation scope "Any workspace": any Notion user can install it, and it is Marketplace-eligible.

evidence.quote: Any workspace (any Notion user can install; Marketplace-eligible)

scopeTiers.text: Only public connections with an installation scope of Any workspace can be listed on the Marketplace.

evidence.quote: Only public connections with an installation scope of Any workspace can be listed on the Marketplace.

scopeTiers.text: Capabilities you can enable: read, update and insert content, read and insert comments, and three levels of user information.

evidence.quote: Capabilities available: Read content, Update content, Insert content, Read comments, Insert comments, and three levels of user information (none, without email addresses, including email addresses).

steps.text: Open the Developer portal and create a new public connection.

evidence.quote: and create a new public connection.

steps.text: Choose OAuth as the authentication method. The other option is an API token, which is limited to one workspace and not Marketplace-eligible.

evidence.quote: OAuth: "User-scoped OAuth 2.0, with access limited to the signed-in user. Supports multiple workspaces and is Marketplace-eligible."
API token: "Workspace-scoped static API token, shared across collaborators, with its own access settings. Limited to 1 workspace and not Marketplace-eligible."

steps.text: Enter your redirect URI and choose the installation scope.

evidence.quote: Fill out the form with your connection details, including your redirect URI(s) under the OAuth configuration section and the connection's installation scope

steps.text: Use the ready-made authorization URL on the connection's page to start the OAuth flow.

evidence.quote: The settings page also showed a ready-made authorization URL with the client ID, response_type=code, owner=user and the redirect URI filled in.

steps.text: Optional: to appear in the Marketplace, submit your listing for review from the Connections listing page.

evidence.quote: When your listing is ready, submit it for review from the **Connections** listing page.

redirectRules.text: Redirect URLs cannot include fragments, relative paths, wildcards or public IP addresses.

evidence.quote: Redirect URLs can't include URL fragments, relative paths, wildcards, or public IP addresses.

redirectRules.text: Notion accepted an http://localhost redirect URI when we registered it.

evidence.quote: We registered http://localhost:3000/api/auth/callback and Notion accepted it.

redirectRules.text: Tested: only the exact registered URI works. A different localhost port failed with "Missing or invalid redirect_uri."

evidence.quote: http://localhost:5555/api/auth/callback (different port) | "Missing or invalid redirect_uri."

redirectRules.text: Tested: an unrelated host is rejected the same way.

evidence.quote: https://example.org/cb (unrelated host) | "Missing or invalid redirect_uri."

requirements.text: Public connections must pass a Notion security review before they can be listed on the Marketplace.

evidence.quote: Public connections must undergo a Notion security review before being listed on the Marketplace.

requirements.text: Creating a connection means agreeing to Notion's Developer Terms.

evidence.quote: By creating a connection, you agree to Notion's Developer Terms.

gotchas.text: The installation scope cannot be changed after you create the connection.

evidence.quote: including your redirect URI(s) under the OAuth configuration section and the connection's installation scope — either Any workspace or Selected workspaces only. This can't be changed after creation.

gotchas.text: Notion now calls integrations "Connections", under Developer tools, so older tutorials use different names.

evidence.quote: Notion calls these Connections, under "Developer tools", next to Workers, Personal access tokens and MCP tokens.
A Notion connection — sometimes called an integration — connects your workspace to external apps and tools.

gotchas.text: In the create dialog, the first click on Create did nothing until the redirect URI had turned into a chip.

evidence.quote: The first click on Create connection did nothing, because the redirect URI had not yet become a chip.

gotchas.text: Notion tells users on the consent screen that it does not review third-party connections.

evidence.quote: Notion does not review third party connections

gotchas.text: Listing on the Marketplace is optional. A public connection works through its OAuth flow without being listed.

evidence.quote: Public connections work independently of Marketplace listings.

gotchas.text: Deleting a connection revokes its access for everyone who installed it.

evidence.quote: Deleting this connection permanently revokes its access for everyone who has installed it

surfaceClaim.text: We created the connection by driving Notion's web developer pages.

evidence.quote: The agent then drove the Notion developer pages in the browser pane.

agentCan.text: Create a connection and set its name, scope and redirect URI.

evidence.quote: Filled the connection name and one redirect URI, then created the connection.

agentCan.text: Test the authorization URL and the redirect rules without authorizing anything.

evidence.quote: Requested Notion's authorization URL three times with different redirect_uri values.

youMust.text: Sign in to Notion. The agent cannot enter credentials.

evidence.quote: Signing in to Notion is the account owner's job.

youMust.text: Agree to the Developer Terms. The agent stopped and asked first.

evidence.quote: Creating a connection means agreeing to Notion's Developer Terms, which needs the account owner's explicit yes.

youMust.text: Each end user must pick pages and approve on the consent screen.

evidence.quote: Each end user must pick pages and approve on the consent screen.

youMust.text: For a Marketplace listing, submit it for review by the Notion team.

evidence.quote: Submit your listing for review by the Notion team.

usualRejections.text: Listings are rejected for reasons ranging from brand or trademark issues to quality concerns to missing baseline criteria. You can fix them and resubmit.

evidence.quote: Connections are rejected for various reasons, from brand/trademark issues to quality concerns to situations where the baseline connection criteria isn't met.

gaps: We did not open the Marketplace submission flow, which opens in a separate tab, so its listing requirements are only what the docs say.
We did not authorize a user, exchange a token, or reveal the client secret.
Only an OAuth connection in a personal workspace was tested, not an organization workspace.
No official support or contact channel for review questions was found in the pages read.
